This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 19.12.2022 passed by IInd MACT, Mandsaur in MACC No.132/2019 on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: The date of accident, negligence and issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal in the case of permanent disability of the claimant a compensation of Rs.12,10,162/- has been awarded by the Tribunal along with interest from the date of claim petition till its realization.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has grossly erred in not considering evidence adduced by appellant in its true prospective.

The Tribunal has erred in considering the income of the appellant on the basis of minimum wages @ Rs.6000/- per month although minimum wages of an unskilled labour in the year 2018 was Rs.7325/- per month.
The Tribunal has grossly erred in assessing the disability of the appellant only at 50% without any reason.

He further submits that appellant requires artificial limb which costs around Rs.1,50,000/- which also needs to be replaced in every 8 to 10 years but Tribunal has grossly erred in not considering that fact while assessing the compensation.
The Tribunal has grossly erred in not awarding just compensation towards general damages like pain and suffering, loss of enjoyment of life and loss of expectancy of life.
Hence, prays for awarding just and proper amount of compensation.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/insurance company supports the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the record it is found that claimant sustained traumatic amputation through right tibia and fibula.
According to the permanent disability certificate Ex.P/105, Tribunal has assessed 50% permanent disability in loss of income.

According to Workmen's Compensation Act Schedule, for the amputation of leg from below knee,
50% permanent disability ought to be assessed for calculating the amount of compensation.
Therefore, from the perusal of the findings of the award it is found that Tribunal has rightly assessed 50% permanent disability with regard to loss of income.
7. Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that Tribunal has wrongly assessed the income of the claimant as Rs.6000/- per month.
According to the circular issued by the Labour Commissioner, Govt. of M.P, the minimum wages prescribed for an unskilled labour for the relevant period was Rs.7325/- per month.
So in the considered opinion of this Court, the just and proper amount of income of the claimant in the present case would be Rs.7325/- per month as per the said circular.

8. Counsel for the appellant further submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on other heads is also on the lower side like loss of enjoyment of life, pain and suffering, attendant charges, special diet, transportation etc.
Perusal of the award it is found that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on other conventional heads is not just and proper.
In the considered opinion of this Court, it would be just and proper in awarding Rs.4,00,000/- on this heads.

9. In view of the above discussion, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be modified and is recalculated as under:

 On all other heads -Rs.4,00,000/-
 --------------

10.

sentences.text: Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.15,07,540/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.12,10,162/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.2,97,378/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
11. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.2,97,378/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
